text:
maria: Quick question — I'm iterating on the "compact mode" for SLO threshold editing in the console. When a tenant sets a soft threshold + quiet window, the current notify preview just says who will be contacted. It doesn't show estimated alert volume or sampling. That's causing product folks to worry about surprises on rollout. Any thoughts on what the preview should surface? :thinking:

alex: Agree we should surface an estimated alert rate. At minimum: est alerts/hour (based on recent telemetry), sample rate, and the fallback tier that will be used if primary route is down. Even a back-of-envelope number is better than nothing. :eyes:

kevin: We can compute a cheap estimate from the 1h/24h rolling counters and a small exponential decay. Something like: recent_rate * breach_prob * 3600. Cheap and fast. Example preview payload:```yaml
preview:
  est_alerts_per_hour: 3.2
  sample_rate: 10%
  fallback: ["pd-team-slo","ops-mail"]
  confidence: low
```

jamie: Two concerns: (1) cost to compute this for every tenant in the UI (esp. list / bulk edit), (2) clarity around per-route overrides — preview must apply tenant defaults, route-level overrides, and any notify suppression rules in the correct order. Otherwise the UX will be misleading.

maria: Good points. For list/bulk view we could show a cached approx value and a "Refresh" button to compute a live estimate. For the order of ops — do we have an established deterministic order in the API? I thought route overrides were applied at runtime after tenant defaults.

alex: Yes, runtime order is: global defaults -> tenant defaults -> route overrides -> runtime suppressions. Preview should mirror that. Also we should show a tiny diff UI: what changes if route override exists (inline).

kevin: Implementation note: add a /v1/slo/preview endpoint that accepts the merged policy object and returns {est_rate, sample_rate, applied_overrides, confidence_hint}. Keep it read-only and rate-limited. That keeps the console simple and avoids coupling heavy logic into frontend.

maria: Sounds reasonable. How expensive will that preview endpoint be? We need it fast enough for modal preview, but also safe behind auth and per-user quotas.

jamie: Make it a best-effort estimate — use precomputed histograms (per-tenant, per-route) updated every minute. If histogram missing, fallback to tenant-level or product-level baselines. Also return a "data_age" field so UI can surface "estimate based on 12m-old stats".

ops-bot: deploy-bot: feature/compact-slo-preview deployed to staging (build 2026.03.20-compact-preview). :rocket:

alex: One UX detail — show an "impact preview" toggle: alerts/hour vs. expected noisy recipients. For noisy tenants, also show a suggested sample rate and a one-click "apply suggestion" that writes a tenant-level sample setting (with audit message).

maria: Love the one-click suggestion. We'll need UX copy to explain tradeoffs (cost vs. visibility). Also add a small "why this number" tooltip linking to the calculation: recent_rate * breach_prob * sample_rate.

kevin: For rollout plan: behind feature flag for 10% of tenants -> monitor alert QPS and false positive rate (we already compute regression metrics). If metrics look good after 48h, expand.

jamie: Acceptance criteria for launch: (1) preview endpoint returns within 1500ms for modal calls, (2) cached list load < 200ms (uses cached approx), (3) feature flag + audit trail for one-click suggestions, (4) console shows data_age + confidence.

maria: I'll draft a short RFC with API contract (payload + example) and the small UX mocks. Posting later today. Thanks all :thumbsup:

alex: Ping me on the RFC, happy to review the API contract.

kevin: I'll prototype the preview handler and histogram fallback logic.

jamie: I'll be on the UX copy + rollout checklist.

maria: Done for now — will @everyone when RFC is up.
